# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

# pr-1140: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session

## Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

Actually wait — could this redaction have been applied to the file IN MY WORKING COPY only (input preparation)? git status says clean, and the file is part of the PR branch. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` showed the redacted strings, so the commit itself contains them. So the PR literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` as test tokens. That's worth a SUGGESTION — use a clearly fake but descriptive value like 'test-access-token' for readability. Not a security issue since it's a mock.

2. The windowed storage walk confirms the "stop, never throw" contract — and notably it does NOT have a cycle guard either. So the cycle exposure is symmetric across both implementations (pre-existing in both). The new code matches the established pattern. Cycle risk: pre-existing pattern, both walks unguarded. Given the PR explicitly hardens against adversarial files, a `visited` set would be cheap. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (pre-existing, symmetric, low realism since writer never creates cycles).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. Is this a real problem? The windowed storage can't know the "newest" record cheaply (it pages), so returning [] is its only option; full-open knows entries.last. The divergence is defensible but the comment overstates ("Same total contract" — total as in never-throws, which IS the same). The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? Returning [] means empty context = the model loses all history silently (bad). Falling back = some history. The PR chose the richer behavior. OK.

3. Now the more serious concern: `getPathToRoot('ghost')` fallback changes semantics for ALL callers, including legit "unknown id" cases that previously got a loud notFound. Who calls getPathToRoot with an externally-influenced id? session_repo.dart:989. Let me look at that call site and session_tree.dart:119 (getBranch(fromId)).

Let me also check: does `Session.buildContextMessages` or anything rely on getPathToRoot throwing for invalid sessions (error propagation paths)? Search for 'notFound' handling.

Also check `setLeafId` — still throws notFound for unknown id (kept). Fine.

4. Cycle: worth flagging.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

Given the PR explicitly hardens against adversarial files, a `visited` set would be cheap. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (pre-existing, symmetric, low realism since writer never creates cycles).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. Is this a real problem? The windowed storage can't know the "newest" record cheaply (it pages), so returning [] is its only option; full-open knows entries.last. The divergence is defensible but the comment overstates ("Same total contract" — total as in never-throws, which IS the same). The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? Returning [] means empty context = the model loses all history silently (bad). Falling back = some history. The PR chose the richer behavior. OK.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

1. The test file at line 635-636 has `accessToken: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` — the literal placeholder IS in the file. Let me see the full context. But wait — was this redaction done by the diff tooling when the PR was created (i.e., the PR itself literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]`)? Let me view the context around those lines. Actually, this redaction marker appearing in the actual checked-out branch file means the PR author's pipeline redacted the token, and the committed test now uses the literal string '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]' as the token. Functionally harmless (mock client), but it's odd — a placeholder leaked into committed code. It still "works" since `.encode()` just base64s it. Is this a real issue? It's cosmetic/quality: a test credential literal reading "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" — awkward but harmless. Actually wait — could this redaction have been applied to the file IN MY WORKING COPY only (input preparation)? git status says clean, and the file is part of the PR branch. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` showed the redacted strings, so the commit itself contains them. So the PR literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` as test tokens. That's worth a SUGGESTION — use a clearly fake but descriptive value like 'test-access-token' for readability. Not a security issue since it's a mock.

2. The windowed storage walk confirms the "stop, never throw" contract — and notably it does NOT have a cycle guard either. So the cycle exposure is symmetric across both implementations (pre-existing in both). The new code matches the established pattern. Cycle risk: pre-existing pattern, both walks unguarded. Given the PR explicitly hardens against adversarial files, a `visited` set would be cheap. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (pre-existing, symmetric, low realism since writer never creates cycles).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. Is this a real problem? The windowed storage can't know the "newest" record cheaply (it pages), so returning [] is its only option; full-open knows entries.last. The divergence is defensible but the comment overstates ("Same total contract" — total as in never-throws, which IS the same). The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? Returning [] means empty context = the model loses all history silently (bad). Falling back = some history. The PR chose the richer behavior. OK.

3. Now the more serious concern: `getPathToRoot('ghost')` fallback changes semantics for ALL callers, including legit "unknown id" cases that previously got a loud notFound. Who calls getPathToRoot with an externally-influenced id? session_repo.dart:989. Let me look at that call site and session_tree.dart:119 (getBranch(fromId)).

Let me also check: does `Session.buildContextMessages` or anything rely on getPathToRoot throwing for invalid sessions (error propagation paths)? Search for 'notFound' handling.

Also check `setLeafId` — still throws notFound for unknown id (kept). Fine.

4. Cycle: worth flagging.

5. `entries.any((entry) => entry.id == leafId)` in the heal — O(n), but only once per open; alternatively could check the byId map which isn't built yet at that point. Fine.

6. The heal runs BEFORE the rewrite; if `fs.writeFile` throws (read-only), healed leaf stays in memory. Fine.

7. One more: the heal happens even when `tornLines.isEmpty` — e.g., a session whose last record is a LeafRecord targeting a legit record: leafId = targetId, exists → no heal. Fine. A LeafRecord with targetId = null → leafId = null → no heal. Fine. A dangling target from a foreign writer → healed. Good.

8. What about `leafIdAfterSessionRecord` for LabelRecord/CompactionRecord → record.id. So compaction sets leaf to compaction record id. Fine, pre-existing.

Now the choke-point guard test: uses `File('lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart')` and `Directory('lib')` relative paths — CWD-dependent. Check whether other tests in the repo read lib sources; grep for "File('lib" or "Directory('lib" in test/.

Also `dart:io` import — check dart_test.yaml platforms.

Let me also check the AC5/verbatim error test: they changed the mock 400 message to the verbatim long string and assert `contains(verbatimError)`. Where does the ErrorEvent message come from? The 400-diagnostic annotation in chatgpt_codex.dart — it embeds the upstream message. The test asserts the annotation includes the full verbatim error plus 'rejected the outbound item/content grammar' and '/compact'. Fine.

AC1 test: 'adversarial corpus' — uses `geminiAssistant` helper (defined earlier in the file, presumably). Note the corpus converts via `responsesInputItems(messages)` twice and asserts equality — "idempotence" claim: converting the same input twice is trivially deterministic; the comment says "re-converting the converted shapes — e.g. codex → another provider → codex" but the test does NOT actually round-trip through another provider; it just calls the same function twice on the same input. That's a weak/misleading assertion — calling a pure function twice with the same args and comparing results tests determinism of the function (which given no randomness is guaranteed) — not idempotence of shapes (which would require responsesInputItems(responsesInputItems(messages) as messages)). The claim in the comment is not what the code does. This is a test-quality finding: the "idempotence" assertion is vacuous. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It's a test asserting something misleading; the actual AC1 property (grammar-valid) is real. I'd call it SUGGESTION (test quality) or IMPORTANT (false confidence)? The PR leans heavily on tests as proof ("now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test"). A vacuous assertion inside the proof test inflates confidence. I'd rate SUGGESTION — the core assertion (grammar violation isNull) is meaningful; the second one is just weak. Hmm, "deterministically" is what the expect reason says — and calling a pure function twice IS a determinism check (weak but not wrong); the COMMENT above it claims E5 idempotence which is overstated. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet

- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` stay `github-actions[bot]`.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
