# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

# pr-1140: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session

## Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

blocks.text:
Interesting findings:

1. The test file at line 635-636 has `accessToken: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` — the literal placeholder IS in the file. Let me see the full context. It's a test with MockClient, so no real network call happens; the token value is inert. But wait — was this redaction done by the diff tooling when the PR was created (i.e., the PR itself literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]`)? Let me view the context around those lines. Actually, this redaction marker appearing in the actual checked-out branch file means the PR author's pipeline redacted the token, and the committed test now uses the literal string '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]' as the token. Functionally harmless (mock client), but it's odd — a placeholder leaked into committed code. It still "works" since `.encode()` just base64s it. Is this a real issue? It's cosmetic/quality: a test credential literal reading "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" — awkward but harmless. Actually wait — could this redaction have been applied to the file IN MY WORKING COPY only (input preparation)? git status says clean, and the file is part of the PR branch. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` showed the redacted strings, so the commit itself contains them. So the PR literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` as test tokens. That's worth a SUGGESTION — use a clearly fake but descriptive value like 'test-access-token' for readability. Not a security issue since it's a mock.

2. The windowed storage walk confirms the "stop, never throw" contract — and notably it does NOT have a cycle guard either. So the cycle exposure is symmetric across both implementations (pre-existing in both). The new code matches the established pattern. Cycle risk: pre-existing pattern, both walks unguarded. Given the PR explicitly hardens against adversarial files, a `visited` set would be cheap. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (pre-existing, symmetric, low realism since writer never creates cycles).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. Is this a real problem? The windowed storage can't know the "newest" record cheaply (it pages), so returning [] is its only option; full-open knows entries.last. The divergence is defensible but the comment overstates ("Same total contract" — total as in never-throws, which IS the same). The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? Returning [] means empty context = the model loses all history silently (bad). Falling back = some history. The PR chose the richer behavior. OK.

3. Now the more serious concern: `getPathToRoot('ghost')` fallback changes semantics for ALL callers, including legit "unknown id" cases that previously got a loud notFound. Who calls getPathToRoot with an externally-influenced id? session_repo.dart:989. Let me look at that call site and session_tree.dart:119 (getBranch(fromId)).

Let me also check: does `Session.buildContextMessages` or anything rely on getPathToRoot throwing for invalid sessions (error propagation paths)? Search for 'notFound' handling.

Also check `setLeafId` — still throws notFound for unknown id (kept). Fine.

4. Cycle: worth flagging.

5. `entries.any((entry) => entry.id == leafId)` in the heal — O(n), but only once per open; alternatively could check the byId map which isn't built yet at that point. Fine.

6. The heal runs BEFORE the rewrite; if `fs.writeFile` throws (read-only), healed leaf stays in memory. Fine.

7. One more: the heal happens even when `tornLines.isEmpty` — e.g., a session whose last record is a LeafRecord targeting a legit record: leafId = targetId, exists → no heal. Fine. A LeafRecord with targetId = null → leafId = null → no heal. Fine. A dangling target from a foreign writer → healed. Good.

8. What about `leafIdAfterSessionRecord` for LabelRecord/CompactionRecord → record.id. So compaction sets leaf to compaction record id. Fine, pre-existing.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

2. The windowed storage walk confirms the "stop, never throw" contract — and notably it does NOT have a cycle guard either. So the cycle exposure is symmetric across both implementations (pre-existing in both). The new code matches the established pattern. Cycle risk: pre-existing pattern, both walks unguarded. Given the PR explicitly hardens against adversarial files, a `visited` set would be cheap. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (pre-existing, symmetric, low realism since writer never creates cycles).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. Is this a real problem? The windowed storage can't know the "newest" record cheaply (it pages), so returning [] is its only option; full-open knows entries.last. The divergence is defensible but the comment overstates ("Same total contract" — total as in never-throws, which IS the same). The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? Returning [] means empty context = the model loses all history silently (bad). Falling back = some history. The PR chose the richer behavior. OK.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

blocks.text:
Interesting findings:

1. The test file at line 635-636 has `accessToken: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` — the literal placeholder IS in the file. Let me see the full context. It's a test with MockClient, so no real network call happens; the token value is inert. But wait — was this redaction done by the diff tooling when the PR was created (i.e., the PR itself literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]`)? Let me view the context around those lines. Actually, this redaction marker appearing in the actual checked-out branch file means the PR author's pipeline redacted the token, and the committed test now uses the literal string '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]' as the token. Functionally harmless (mock client), but it's odd — a placeholder leaked into committed code. It still "works" since `.encode()` just base64s it. Is this a real issue? It's cosmetic/quality: a test credential literal reading "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" — awkward but harmless. Actually wait — could this redaction have been applied to the file IN MY WORKING COPY only (input preparation)? git status says clean, and the file is part of the PR branch. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` showed the redacted strings, so the commit itself contains them. So the PR literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` as test tokens. That's worth a SUGGESTION — use a clearly fake but descriptive value like 'test-access-token' for readability. Not a security issue since it's a mock.

2. The windowed storage walk confirms the "stop, never throw" contract — and notably it does NOT have a cycle guard either. So the cycle exposure is symmetric across both implementations (pre-existing in both). The new code matches the established pattern. Cycle risk: pre-existing pattern, both walks unguarded. Given the PR explicitly hardens against adversarial files, a `visited` set would be cheap. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (pre-existing, symmetric, low realism since writer never creates cycles).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. Is this a real problem? The windowed storage can't know the "newest" record cheaply (it pages), so returning [] is its only option; full-open knows entries.last. The divergence is defensible but the comment overstates ("Same total contract" — total as in never-throws, which IS the same). The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? Returning [] means empty context = the model loses all history silently (bad). Falling back = some history. The PR chose the richer behavior. OK.

3. Now the more serious concern: `getPathToRoot('ghost')` fallback changes semantics for ALL callers, including legit "unknown id" cases that previously got a loud notFound. Who calls getPathToRoot with an externally-influenced id? session_repo.dart:989. Let me look at that call site and session_tree.dart:119 (getBranch(fromId)).

Let me also check: does `Session.buildContextMessages` or anything rely on getPathToRoot throwing for invalid sessions (error propagation paths)? Search for 'notFound' handling.

Also check `setLeafId` — still throws notFound for unknown id (kept). Fine.

4. Cycle: worth flagging.

5. `entries.any((entry) => entry.id == leafId)` in the heal — O(n), but only once per open; alternatively could check the byId map which isn't built yet at that point. Fine.

6. The heal runs BEFORE the rewrite; if `fs.writeFile` throws (read-only), healed leaf stays in memory. Fine.

7. One more: the heal happens even when `tornLines.isEmpty` — e.g., a session whose last record is a LeafRecord targeting a legit record: leafId = targetId, exists → no heal. Fine. A LeafRecord with targetId = null → leafId = null → no heal. Fine. A dangling target from a foreign writer → healed. Good.

8. What about `leafIdAfterSessionRecord` for LabelRecord/CompactionRecord → record.id. So compaction sets leaf to compaction record id. Fine, pre-existing.

Now the choke-point guard test: uses `File('lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart')` and `Directory('lib')` relative paths — CWD-dependent. Check whether other tests in the repo read lib sources; grep for "File('lib" or "Directory('lib" in test/.

Also `dart:io` import — check dart_test.yaml platforms.

Let me also check the AC5/verbatim error test: they changed the mock 400 message to the verbatim long string and assert `contains(verbatimError)`. Where does the ErrorEvent message come from? The 400-diagnostic annotation in chatgpt_codex.dart — it embeds the upstream message. The test asserts the annotation includes the full verbatim error plus 'rejected the outbound item/content grammar' and '/compact'. Fine.

AC1 test: 'adversarial corpus' — uses `geminiAssistant` helper (defined earlier in the file, presumably). Note the corpus converts via `responsesInputItems(messages)` twice and asserts equality — "idempotence" claim: converting the same input twice is trivially deterministic; the comment says "re-converting the converted shapes — e.g. codex → another provider → codex" but the test does NOT actually round-trip through another provider; it just calls the same function twice on the same input. That's a weak/misleading assertion — calling a pure function twice with the same args and comparing results tests determinism of the function (which given no randomness is guaranteed) — not idempotence of shapes (which would require responsesInputItems(responsesInputItems(messages) as messages)). The claim in the comment is not what the code does. This is a test-quality finding: the "idempotence" assertion is vacuous. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It's a test asserting something misleading; the actual AC1 property (grammar-valid) is real. I'd call it SUGGESTION (test quality) or IMPORTANT (false confidence)? The PR leans heavily on tests as proof ("now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test"). A vacuous assertion inside the proof test inflates confidence. I'd rate SUGGESTION — the core assertion (grammar violation isNull) is meaningful; the second one is just weak. Hmm, "deterministically" is what the expect reason says — and calling a pure function twice IS a determinism check (weak but not wrong); the COMMENT above it claims E5 idempotence which is overstated. I'll flag as SUGGESTION with clear explanation.

Also in the corpus test: `ToolResultMessage(content: content...)` with `result('', const [])` — empty call id + empty content. And 'empty-records' includes `UserMessage.text('')`. These check converter totality. Good.

Now — does the property test actually verify "grammar-valid" strongly? `firstResponsesGrammarViolation(input)` — a repo-provided validator. Fine.

Next: the poison fixture test writes a raw line via `fs.appendFile` and expects quarantine. The poison line uses 'message' record with content type 'function_call' — SessionRecord.fromJson throws FormatException → parseSessionLines yields null → tornLines. Good.

It appends to file & index; _currentLeafId = 'r1'. Then reopened: parses lines; 'rp' torn; entries r0, r1; leafId after loop = 'r1' (r1 is last valid). Heal: 'r1' in entries → no heal needed. getLeafId → 'r1'. buildContextMessages → getPathToRoot('r1') → r1 →…

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd

🚨 **IMPORTANT (unchanged code — no diff line to anchor): the leaf heal is missing from `WindowedSessionStorage`**

The fix heals the tracked leaf in `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked` when the leaf record (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`) was quarantined. `WindowedSessionStorage` — the resume path for large/marathon sessions — has the same exposure and was not touched:

- `windowed_session_storage.dart:67` / `:612` / `:646` set `_currentLeafId = leafIdAfterSessionRecord(chunk.entries.last.record)`; for a trailing `LeafRecord` whose `targetId` was torn/quarantined, that id dangles exactly as in #858.
- `getLeafId()` (line 879) returns the dangling id without throwing (fine), but `getPathToRoot` returns `[]` for the unknown id (the walk never starts), so `SessionTree.getBranch()` yields an **empty branch** and the resume proceeds with silently empty context — no brick, but silent total history loss for that turn, i.e. the same user harm this card set out to eliminate.
- `SessionTree._append` then parents new records on the dangling id, so the hole persists for the session's lifetime; `_branchBottomId` also goes stale (`_ingestAtTail` finds no re-anchor point).

Reachability is the same poison shape the new tests cover: a malformed line near the tail plus a trailing record referencing it — but through the windowed open used for big sessions. The full-open heal ports directly: when `leafIdAfterSessionRecord(chunk.entries.last.record)` is not resolvable among resident records, fall back to `chunk.entries.last.record.id`.

Not blocking (pre-existing behavior; the windowed walk already honored "stop, never throw"), but the PR's headline claim — "no replayable history may ever brick a session" — currently holds only on the full-open path. Either mirror the heal here or record the gap on the card as an explicit follow-up.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (comments)

**Summary**: Resume-side fix is correct and well-tested: the leaf heal + stop-at-hole walk match the windowed storage's total contract, the two old throwing-contract tests were properly replaced, `dart analyze` is clean, and all touched suites pass locally (test/session: 20 ✅, chatgpt_codex_test: 25 ✅). No blocking issues. Ticket ACs AC1–AC5 are each backed by a test verified in this checkout; one sub-claim is overstated (below).

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 IMPORTANT — the same dangling-leaf shape is **not healed in `WindowedSessionStorage`** (unchanged code, so noted here): torn tail + trailing `LeafRecord` ⇒ silently empty-context resume on the large-session path. Detail: `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5_windowed_gap.md`
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — the AC1 test's "Idempotence (E5)" assertion is vacuous (re-runs the same pure function on the same input); the E5 "convert-twice" claim is not actually exercised. → `comment1.md`
- 💡 SUGGESTION — committed test credentials are literal `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` placeholders (`session_storage_test.dart:635`); use descriptive fakes. → `comment2.md`
- 💡 SUGGESTION — `parentId` cycle still hangs the walk (pre-existing; visited-set makes it truly total). → `comment3.md`
- 💡 SUGGESTION — the silent heal/fallback paths are unobservable; consider a `leafHealed` flag / timingLog line. → `comment4.md`

**Next Steps**:
1. Mirror the leaf heal in `WindowedSessionStorage` (or document the gap on #858 as follow-up).
2. Replace the vacuous E5 assertion with a real wire→Message round-trip, or drop the claim.
3. Optionally swap the `[REDACTED]` placeholders and add the cycle guard.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the

- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet

);

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1140
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1140
- **Title**: fix(#858): Codex/Responses wire — no replayable history may ever brick a session
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-858` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +428
- **Deletions**: -57
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:52:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-01T00:29:26Z

## PR Description

Fixes #858

## Capability surface (per the card)

| Source of `input` items | Status in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| `responsesInputItems(history)` conversion | **Already total on main** (landed 2026-09-21, ab98dff3a) — now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test: poison call, thinking-only (E2), image-only assistant + tool result, orphan results, merged roles, empty records, steering interleave (E3), compaction-split pair (E4), codex-authored tails with convert-twice idempotence (E5). |
| Replay/passthrough of stored raw response items (OQ1 prime suspect) | **None exists.** Grep audit: the only `input` assembly site in the codex adapter is `_requestBody()` → `responsesInputItems(downgradeUnsupportedImages(...))`; `responsesInputItems` is referenced nowhere else in `lib/`. Now guarded by the AC4 choke-point REG test (single `'input':` key, exactly two converter uses — request body + 400 annotation, no other lib file references the converter). |
| Reasoning/`encrypted_content` replay items | No such wire items are emitted today (`lib/` has zero `encrypted_content` references); thinking blocks ride no wire slot. Under the property test's grammar check. |
| Steering/mid-turn injected messages | Flow through the converter as any user message — covered as a corpus case (E3). |
| Resume/compaction/branch-summary records | Degrade to valid items (compaction/branch summaries project to user messages; an orphan `function_call_output` from a compaction cut is emitted **top-level**, never as a content part — E4 test). |

## The actual brick found (and fixed)

Not on the wire — on the **resume side**. `JsonlSessionStorage.open` quarantines
a malformed JSONL line (correct, "never fatal"), but surviving records still
reference the dropped record via `parentId` (or a `LeafRecord.targetId`), and
`getPathToRoot` **threw `Entry <id> not found`** on the hole — permanently,
because the quarantine rewrite had already removed the record from the file.
Every future resume of such a session failed: a genuinely replayable history
bricking the session. The windowed storage's walk already had the total
contract ("window edge: stop, never throw"); the full-open storage now matches:

- `getPathToRoot` stops at a hole; a dangling leaf id falls back to the newest
  surviving record's chain — never throws;
- the tracked leaf is healed at load when its record was quarantined;
- `getLeafId` no longer throws on a dangling id.

Two pre-existing tests pinned the old throwing contract; they are replaced by
the new total-contract tests (per the goal card, the throw IS the brick).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — adversarial-corpus property test (pure): `chatgpt_codex_test.dart` "adversarial corpus: every authored/poisoned/degenerate shape converts grammar-valid".
- **AC2** — poison fixture → grammar-valid items + simulated turn vs fake Responses stream: session-side "poison-typed session resumes a full turn without any JSONL rewrite" + the pre-existing gemini-switch turn test.
- **AC3** — resume-without-rewrite byte-compare: same test, `expect(file, before)` after the turn.
- **AC4** — choke-point guard (REG): "choke-point guard (#858 AC4)".
- **AC5** — 400 diagnostic: the verbatim `git/references` error string (`Invalid value: 'function_call'. Supported values are: 'input_text', 'input_image', 'input_audio', 'output_text', 'refusal', 'input_file', 'computer_screenshot', 'summary_text', and 'encrypted_content'.`) pinned on the annotated error event.

## Delta note vs the 9/23 card

- The card's wire threats were addressed by #705 (merged 2026-09-21) before this card's bulk re-assignment; this PR proves totality (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 + E1–E5) rather than re-patching the converter, per the card's own OQ1 shrink clause.
- OQ2: the 9/23 `fa` binary postdates #705's merge, so the observed 9/24 brick cannot be explained by the wire converter alone; the resume-side quarantine brick found here is a concrete, reproduced mechanism by which replayable history still bricked sessions on current main (pre-fix probes fail with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`). A version/wire-grammar stamp in diagnostics (second tier) is **not added**: the annotation already names the suspect outbound item and the recovery path; a stamp adds nothing without a wire-grammar revision.
- One deliberate scope note: the converter drops (rather than wire-encodes) `ImageContent` in user messages even for vision-capable models — pre-#705 behavior, content-loss-but-safe, unchanged here (out of card scope).

## Verification

- `dart test test/session/ test/providers/chatgpt_codex_test.dart test/providers/codex_transport_test.dart` — 288 passed.
- `dart test test/compaction/ test/task/` — 466 passed (getBranch consumers).
- `dart test test/ttsr/ test/trajectory/` — 237 passed.
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files — clean.
- Brick regression demonstrated pre-fix: the new tests fail on origin/main's `session_storage.dart` with exactly `SessionException: Entry rp not found`, pass post-fix.
- No touches to `transient_retry_stream.dart` / `provider_common.dart` (#1132 overlap avoided).

blocks.text:
Interesting findings:

1. The test file at line 635-636 has `accessToken: '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'` — the literal placeholder IS in the file. Let me see the full context. It's a test with MockClient, so no real network call happens; the token value is inert. But wait — was this redaction done by the diff tooling when the PR was created (i.e., the PR itself literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]`)? Let me view the context around those lines. Actually, this redaction marker appearing in the actual checked-out branch file means the PR author's pipeline redacted the token, and the committed test now uses the literal string '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]' as the token. Functionally harmless (mock client), but it's odd — a placeholder leaked into committed code. It still "works" since `.encode()` just base64s it. Is this a real issue? It's cosmetic/quality: a test credential literal reading "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" — awkward but harmless. Actually wait — could this redaction have been applied to the file IN MY WORKING COPY only (input preparation)? git status says clean, and the file is part of the PR branch. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` showed the redacted strings, so the commit itself contains them. So the PR literally contains `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` as test tokens. That's worth a SUGGESTION — use a clearly fake but descriptive value like 'test-access-token' for readability. Not a security issue since it's a mock.

2. The windowed storage walk confirms the "stop, never throw" contract — and notably it does NOT have a cycle guard either. So the cycle exposure is symmetric across both implementations (pre-existing in both). The new code matches the established pattern. Cycle risk: pre-existing pattern, both walks unguarded. Given the PR explicitly hardens against adversarial files, a `visited` set would be cheap. I'll flag as SUGGESTION (pre-existing, symmetric, low realism since writer never creates cycles).

But the windowed walk returns `path` even when leafId is unknown — it returns [] if `_byId[leafId]` is null and not in appendedBelow! Look:

```dart
var current = _byId[leafId] ?? _appendedBelow[leafId];
while (current != null) { ... }
return path.reversed.toList();
```

If leafId is unknown → current == null → while skipped → returns []. So the windowed walk returns [] for a dangling leaf, while the full-open walk now falls back to the newest record's chain. The PR comment says "Same total contract as the windowed storage's walk" — but they're NOT identical: windowed returns [], full-open falls back to newest. Slight semantic divergence between the two implementations of the same interface. Callers switching storage implementations (windowed vs full) get different context for the same dangling id. Is this a real problem? The windowed storage can't know the "newest" record cheaply (it pages), so returning [] is its only option; full-open knows entries.last. The divergence is defensible but the comment overstates ("Same total contract" — total as in never-throws, which IS the same). The comment says "stop, never throw" which is about not throwing, so it's fair. Hmm — but is falling back to the newest record's chain actually SAFER than returning []? Returning [] means empty context = the model loses all history silently (bad). Falling back = some history. The PR chose the richer behavior. OK.

3. Now the more serious concern: `getPathToRoot('ghost')` fallback changes semantics for ALL callers, including legit "unknown id" cases that previously got a loud notFound. Who calls getPathToRoot with an externally-influenced id? session_repo.dart:989. Let me look at that call site and session_tree.dart:119 (getBranch(fromId)).

Let me also check: does `Session.buildContextMessages` or anything rely on getPathToRoot throwing for invalid sessions (error propagation paths)? Search for 'notFound' handling.

Also check `setLeafId` — still throws notFound for unknown id (kept). Fine.

4. Cycle: worth flagging.

5. `entries.any((entry) => entry.id == leafId)` in the heal — O(n), but only once per open; alternatively could check the byId map which isn't built yet at that point. Fine.

6. The heal runs BEFORE the rewrite; if `fs.writeFile` throws (read-only), healed leaf stays in memory. Fine.

7. One more: the heal happens even when `tornLines.isEmpty` — e.g., a session whose last record is a LeafRecord targeting a legit record: leafId = targetId, exists → no heal. Fine. A LeafRecord with targetId = null → leafId = null → no heal. Fine. A dangling target from a foreign writer → healed. Good.

8. What about `leafIdAfterSessionRecord` for LabelRecord/CompactionRecord → record.id. So compaction sets leaf to compaction record id. Fine, pre-existing.

Now the choke-point guard test: uses `File('lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart')` and `Directory('lib')` relative paths — CWD-dependent. Check whether other tests in the repo read lib sources; grep for "File('lib" or "Directory('lib" in test/.

Also `dart:io` import — check dart_test.yaml platforms.

Let me also check the AC5/verbatim error test: they changed the mock 400 message to the verbatim long string and assert `contains(verbatimError)`. Where does the ErrorEvent message come from? The 400-diagnostic annotation in chatgpt_codex.dart — it embeds the upstream message. The test asserts the annotation includes the full verbatim error plus 'rejected the outbound item/content grammar' and '/compact'. Fine.

AC1 test: 'adversarial corpus' — uses `geminiAssistant` helper (defined earlier in the file, presumably). Note the corpus converts via `responsesInputItems(messages)` twice and asserts equality — "idempotence" claim: converting the same input twice is trivially deterministic; the comment says "re-converting the converted shapes — e.g. codex → another provider → codex" but the test does NOT actually round-trip through another provider; it just calls the same function twice on the same input. That's a weak/misleading assertion — calling a pure function twice with the same args and comparing results tests determinism of the function (which given no randomness is guaranteed) — not idempotence of shapes (which would require responsesInputItems(responsesInputItems(messages) as messages)). The claim in the comment is not what the code does. This is a test-quality finding: the "idempotence" assertion is vacuous. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It's a test asserting something misleading; the actual AC1 property (grammar-valid) is real. I'd call it SUGGESTION (test quality) or IMPORTANT (false confidence)? The PR leans heavily on tests as proof ("now proven by the AC1 adversarial-corpus property test"). A vacuous assertion inside the proof test inflates confidence. I'd rate SUGGESTION — the core assertion (grammar violation isNull) is meaningful; the second one is just weak. Hmm, "deterministically" is what the expect reason says — and calling a pure function twice IS a determinism check (weak but not wrong); the COMMENT above it claims E5 idempotence which is overstated. I'll flag as SUGGESTION with clear explanation.

Also in the corpus test: `ToolResultMessage(content: content...)` with `result('', const [])` — empty call id + empty content. And 'empty-records' includes `UserMessage.text('')`. These check converter totality. Good.

Now — does the property test actually verify "grammar-valid" strongly? `firstResponsesGrammarViolation(input)` — a repo-provided validator. Fine.

Next: the poison fixture test writes a raw line via `fs.appendFile` and expects quarantine. The poison line uses 'message' record with content type 'function_call' — SessionRecord.fromJson throws FormatException → parseSessionLines yields null → tornLines. Good.

Wait, one important check in the first test: after `createStorage()` they append r0, then raw poison line 'rp' parented r0, then r1 parented 'rp' — `storage.appendEntry` for r1: appendEntry does NOT validate parentId! It appends to file & index; _currentLeafId = 'r1'. Then reopened: parses lines; 'rp' torn; entries r0, r1; leafId after loop = 'r1' (r1 is last valid). Heal: 'r1' in entries → no heal needed. getLeafId → 'r1'. buildContextMessages → getPathToRoot('r1') → r1 →…

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd
  invocation, marker-parity with the CI `guards` job (which also runs it
